raw.assessment: The incumbent performs relatively well when assignments remain unchanged: median handling is seven minutes, versus 17 overall. Transition-linked selection or reconciliation errors are plausible because all eight affected exports involved assignment changes or renames, but causation is unproven. Execution takes only 40–75 seconds; replacement delays therefore do not establish slow generation. The concrete isolation limit is D1-O4: zero observed cross-center rows excludes the recently split-course center and cannot establish safety for that transition.

openings.claim: Resolving requested-week course membership through current assignments or mutable names may explain transition-linked omissions. Stable course identity with explicitly defined week membership is a candidate correction.
openings.delta: Move the investigation from rerunning exports to identifying which selection rule changes the intended course set.
openings.prediction: Holding attendance and the coordinator-confirmed intended set fixed, assignment changes or renames alter current output membership; a week-aware identity rule removes that difference. Absence of this effect weakens the hypothesis.
openings.probe: In private staging with fabricated participants, compare unchanged, reassigned, renamed and split-course fixtures against explicit expected sets. Include a second center and inspect every exported row for authorized-center membership. Preserve the documented CSV schema and verify concurrent attendance entry. Time-box diagnosis and any candidate implementation within six engineer-days and existing hosting.
assumptions: Historical membership may be unavailable; reconstruction feasibility must be established before selecting this correction.
Split-course membership needs an explicit expected result rather than inferred name matching.

openings.claim: Does excess coordinator handling arise primarily from course-set reconciliation, spreadsheet import, or repeated replacement requests?
openings.delta: Distinguish active handling from elapsed replacement delay before choosing a workflow change.
openings.prediction: If reconciliation dominates, observed checking and correction consume most excess active time. If import dominates, those steps remain costly even with a confirmed-correct course set; replacement waiting alone does not explain active handling.
openings.probe: Use the six coordinators’ two short sessions with fabricated CSVs in authorized workspaces. Counterbalance confirmed-correct and transition-affected files; timestamp checking, correction, downloading, importing and requests separately, recording waiting separately. Compare intended sets with each coordinator’s actual schedule source.
assumptions: These sessions diagnose mechanisms; the next 40 exports must separately establish the stated success measures.

raw.assessment: The exporter may generate replacement demand by organizing past attendance through current assignments and changeable course names. Observed associations do not establish either feedback edge. The sampled absence of cross-center rows does not establish safety for the untested course split.

openings.claim: Using current instructor assignments for a requested week may alter course selection after attendance was entered, producing apparent omissions, replacement requests, and repeated checking.
openings.delta: Treat replacement demand as potentially created by the exporter's temporal model; test course selection against relationships relevant to the requested week.
openings.prediction: Holding attendance and the intended course set constant, changing only the current instructor assignment changes the incumbent export's membership. A week-specific selection rule prevents that change. If membership stays constant, this selection mechanism is weakened.
openings.probe: Replay fabricated reassignment cases in staging against coordinator-agreed intended sets, comparing membership before and after reassignment under both rules. Preserve center authorization, documented CSV and concurrent attendance entry; stop implementation exploration at six engineer-days and the hosting allowance.
assumptions: Instructor assignment influences export selection, not merely labels.
Week-relevant relationships can be recovered within the resource limit; this is unestablished.

openings.claim: Does presenting renamed courses without their prior names generate false omission reports and replacement requests even when the intended records are present?
openings.delta: Test a feedback edge from course-name presentation to reconciliation demand, independently of actual selection errors.
openings.prediction: For identical correct CSVs, an accompanying course-name mapping reduces false omission reports and checking time. Unchanged reports, or demonstrated missing records, weaken the presentation explanation.
openings.probe: Use the six coordinators' two short sessions for counterbalanced fabricated rename exercises with and without a private current/prior-name manifest. Observe checking time, import completion and replacement decisions; keep CSV bytes identical. Fit mock preparation within the shared six-day limit without production locks or extra hosting.
assumptions: An accurate name mapping can be supplied for the exercise.
Fabricated exercises can reveal behavior but cannot establish the next-40-export success measure.

openings.claim: Current assignments or mutable names may distort requested-week membership, creating omissions and repeated checking.
openings.discriminator: With attendance and intended sets fixed, reassignment or rename changes membership; week-aware stable identity prevents this.
openings.probe: Compare unchanged, reassigned, renamed and split-course fixtures in private staging; agree expected split membership, inspect every row across two centers, verify concurrent attendance entry.
openings.uncertainty: Association is not causation; historical relationships may be unavailable. Sampled isolation excludes the split center.

openings.claim: Excess handling may arise from reconciliation, import or repeated replacement requests.
openings.discriminator: Checking/correction dominates versus import remaining costly for confirmed-correct files; waiting differs from active handling.
openings.probe: Counterbalance correct and affected fabricated files in six coordinators' two sessions; time checking, correction, downloading, importing and requests separately from waiting; compare actual schedule sources.
openings.uncertainty: Timetable accuracy and fabricated-task realism remain unknown.

openings.claim: Renamed-course presentation may trigger false omissions despite complete records.
openings.discriminator: A private prior/current-name mapping reduces checking and replacement decisions for identical correct CSVs.
openings.probe: Counterbalance rename exercises with/without mapping in the shared sessions; observe import completion too.
openings.uncertainty: Requires accurate mapping; actual missing records or unchanged reports weaken this explanation.

lineage.reason: With A1; preserves identity, rename-selection and split distinctions.
With Z1; preserves temporal selection and replacement-demand mechanism.
Presentation can fail independently of selection.

post_distill.decision: Diagnose before choosing correction. Keep participant names private and authorized, documented CSV supported, attendance entry available, and combined work within six engineer-days/existing hosting. Synthetic sessions cannot establish success: assess next 40 exports against median handling <=12 minutes, >=95% intended sets, and zero cross-center records.
